recognize_zh: 骨髓抹片中巨噬細胞旁可見一群小型、呈臘腸狀或橢圓形、中央有橫隔（transverse septum）的酵母樣菌體，部分成雙排列；這種以分裂而非出芽繁殖的橫隔菌體是馬尼菲青黴菌（Talaromyces/Penicillium marneffei）的特徵。
features: Clusters of small (about 2-6 micron) oval to elongated sausage-shaped yeast-like organisms
Organisms show a central transverse septum/bipolar staining, dividing by fission rather than budding
Organisms lie adjacent to and within vacuolated macrophage cytoplasm
Macrophages and myeloid precursors with coarse granules in the background
Image is slightly out of focus, limiting fine structural detail
describe_en: Bone marrow aspirate smear (Wright-Giemsa, oil immersion) shows clusters of small oval to elongated, sausage-shaped yeast-like organisms, several with a distinct central transverse septum, located adjacent to and within macrophages. No budding forms or capsules are appreciated, although focus is suboptimal. Background marrow elements include macrophages and granulated myeloid precursors. Findings are consistent with Talaromyces (Penicillium) marneffei infection; confirmation by fungal culture (red diffusible pigment at 25 C) and GMS/PAS stains is recommended.

ddx.vs: Histoplasma yeasts are uniform, round to oval, 2-4 micron with a pseudocapsular halo and narrow-based budding, lacking a transverse septum.
Amastigotes have a nucleus plus a rod-shaped kinetoplast instead of a septum, and are not GMS positive.
Candida shows budding yeasts and pseudohyphae without transverse septation.
Storage histiocytes contain fibrillar or crystalline material without discrete organisms with a septum.
